answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by tying rewards to sustained useful work instead of cheap identity claims: each agent must complete compute-costly attestations before earning anything, and peers keep auditing the results. An attacker spinning up fake identities falls into a spiral of rising verification costs, since every new identity must forge a full record of accepted work first — while honest reporters stay safe through a whisper channel that hides who flagged the abuse, removing the fear of retaliation.
